request.spec:
A button downloads the period figures as a CSV file: a header line person,period,figure,carried
then one line per person and period, people in list order and periods in the order added, with the
figures as the rows show them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the period figures as a CSV file: a header line person,period,figure,carried
then one line per person and period, people in list order and periods in the order added, with the
figures as the rows show them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an **Export period figures (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-periods"`) in the Periods area. It downloads `periods.csv`, which starts with the header `person,period,figure,carried` and then has one line per person and period. All four tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the export test and the three other scenarios.

- **Front end** (`src/main/frontend/features/periods/export.slot.tsx`): before writing the file, the button re-reads periods, people, claims and rates from the store. The figure and carried values come from the same functions the person rows use, so the file matches the screen. That includes closed periods keeping the figures they had when closed. Names containing a comma are quoted, so "Lee, Jo" comes out as `"Lee, Jo"`.
- **People order:** people are listed in the stored list order and retired people are included, the same as the existing people export. The file ignores the on-screen sort and the "show retired" checkbox.
- **Period order:** the app only kept periods sorted by from-date, with no record of when each was added. To get "the order added" I made three changes:
  - A new migration, `V99__period_added.sql`, gives each period an `added` number that goes up with each one added. It's also kept in the period history, as the other period columns are.
  - The periods endpoint now returns that number (`Periods.added`, `PeriodResponse`, `RespondWithPeriods`), and the export sorts by it.
  - Cloning a sheet now copies its periods in the order they were added.

The tests only add periods in date order, so they don't check this ordering. Periods that existed before the migration get numbers in whatever order the database fills them in, so their original order can't be recovered.
